title: Field-extension exchange morphism isomorphism
statement:
Let $L/K$ be an extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension] and let $g:T\to S$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] morphism of schemes over $K$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. For $W=T,S$ put $W_L=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}L$ and let $r_W:W_L\to W$ be the scalar-extension projection [def-pc-base-change]. Write $g_L:T_L\to S_L$ for the induced base change of $g$, so that the square with sides $g,g_L,r_T,r_S$ is cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

Let $E\in\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ be a bounded below derived object of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] whose cohomology sheaves have geometric stalks torsion of orders invertible in $K$ [def-kun-torsion-invertible]. Put $E_L=r_T^{-1}E$, using the derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], and use the derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then the canonical derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] for this cartesian field-extension square,
$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{g,L,E}:r_S^{-1}Rg_*E\longrightarrow Rg_{L,*}E_L,
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Dplus((S_L)_{\Et})$.

source.place: Lemma 0F1C (lemma-base-change-field-extension), statement and proof: the smooth-base-change comparison map for the field-extension square

proof.text: Construct M as the relative perfect closure of L in its algebraic closure. Give M its composite K-algebra structure and put P=perfectClosure K M. Both fields are perfect; P/K and M/L are purely inseparable, and the algebra structures form the two compatible towers required by the comparison lemma. These are concrete Mathlib constructions.

Every finitely generated intermediate extension of M/P has a separating transcendence basis because P is perfect. Hence M/P is separable in the general field-extension sense. Pull E back to T_P. The exact-functor homology comparison and the inverse-image stalk comparison identify every geometric cohomology stalk with its original stalk at the image point. Transport each elementwise annihilator through this abelian-group isomorphism and through K to P. The pullback cancellation square for g_P gives qcqs by base-change stability.

Apply the separable exchange theorem to M/P,g_P,E_P and the coefficient condition just proved. Apply the reverse implication of the purely inseparable comparison to transfer its invertibility to the original specified exchange for L/K.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0F1C: concrete relative perfect closures, exact homology and geometric-stalk transport, separable smooth-limit exchange, and proved purely inseparable comparison; no new unresolved theorem.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement and all its coefficient and qcqs hypotheses. Proved the separable case by the existing canonical smooth-limit base-change theorem, constructing the smooth system over S rather than assuming T is qcqs over K. Constructed compatible perfect closures inside a perfect purely inseparable overfield, used the existing separating-basis leaf for separability, and made the universal-homeomorphism reduction identify the canonical maps via the mate lemma and the existing horizontal-pasting formula. Reused all facts from existing nodes, with no new nodes and no Lean attachment; repeated Mathlib searches found no match. Second reading expands the affine transition check and both purely inseparable comparison arguments, with no statement change or new dependency.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the first sentence of the proof of lem-kun-0f1h-sep-reduction, which applies field-extension base change to j and h. Steps 2--3 and 4--9 expand the separable and perfect-closure cases, respectively, of the existing blueprint lem-kun-0f1c; the comparison map is identified explicitly. The chapter and unit route are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses the generic composition isomorphism to identify the geometric stalk after scalar extension; the unit has no separate inverse-image pseudofunctor construction.
Step 2 uses only its general smooth-morphism base-change clause to construct the smooth inverse system over S, not its properness clause or a Picard argument.
Step 6 uses its assertion for every K-scheme to prove universal homeomorphism of purely inseparable scalar extension; this is the topological tool explicitly required by the field-perfection route.
Step 7 uses the general equivalence of etale topoi under universal homeomorphisms, exactly as required by Tag 0F1C; it replaces no step of the Kunneth route.
Step 8 uses the general categorical criterion to show the mate is invertible when both horizontal inverse images are equivalences; the unit has no theorem with these precise mate hypotheses.
Step 8 needs the generic bounded below inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions to instantiate the mate criterion and the exchange definition.
